chunks: As regards your reference to the question of equality (in distribution of shares from the Muslim common fund),

this is a matter in which I have not taken a decision by my own opinion, nor have I done it by my caprice. But I found, and you too (must have) found, that whatever the Prophet - may Allāh bless him and his descendants - brought had been finalised.
Therefore, I felt no need to turn towards you about a share which had been determined by Allāh and in which His verdict has been passed.
By Allāh, in this matter, therefore, you two or anyone else can have no favour from me.
May Allāh keep our hearts and your hearts in righteousness, and may He grant us and you endurance.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali justify his independent decision-making in governance without consulting the companions?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) asserts that his distribution of wealth was not a matter of personal discretion but followed the established precedent of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), rendering further consultation unnecessary. This response underscores the Shia principle of *Sunnah* as the binding framework for governance, distinguishing between the Prophet's finality in establishing norms and the Imam's role in implementing them without arbitrary change. By stating 'God has taken our hearts and yours to the truth,' he emphasizes divine guidance in leadership decisions, a key theme in understanding the legitimacy of the Ahl al-Bayt's authority.
